name: ramose
description: Ramose — an immutable, Datomic-inspired graph database for Cloudflare (Workers + Durable Objects + R2), built on Effect. One package: the schema and client (`ramose/db`), the Alchemy resources (`ramose`), the peer Worker (`ramose/worker`), the React hooks (`ramose/react`) and the Better Auth plugins (`ramose/better-auth`).
author: Tyler van Hensbergen <tvanhens@gmail.com>
//dependencies: Ramose owns its whole runtime graph on purpose: `bun add ramose` has to be
enough for the portable and deploy paths.
`effect` — a bare `effect` in a consumer's manifest installs 3.x, which is
the wrong major. Owning the dependency with a prerelease floor makes the
Effect 4 line resolve without the consumer typing `effect@rc`. The floor
carries a prerelease tag so semver admits the other 4.0.0 prereleases;
`<5.0.0` keeps the next major out.
App `Db` methods are promises and subscriptions. Effect types live only on
`db.effect.*`, `ramose/db/effect`, and `ramose/effect` (the opt-in hatch).
Two copies of `effect` in one tree produce two mutually unassignable sets
of types — that failure is confined to the hatch and the deploy surface,
not the promise-first app path. A consumer never has to name `effect`:
it arrives under `ramose`, and `ramose/effect` re-exports the same module
instances for resolvers that do not hoist (pnpm's default, Yarn PnP). A
consumer who *does* add `effect` should use a range compatible with this
one; anything else is the one way back to two copies.
`alchemy` is a real dependency, not a peer: it carries the `alchemy` CLI
the quickstart runs. Its types sit in the public deploy signatures, and
the 2.x line is still beta (no semver signal). The range is pinned to the
tested beta and bumped per release — not `>=x <3`, which would admit
every future 2.x beta. The workspace root pins the same tested version
(exact) so `bun update alchemy` cannot split two copies.
React is an optional peer — a server-only app needs none of it. So are
`better-auth` and `zod`, which only `ramose/better-auth` touches. Apps
using that subpath need both peers installed. The zod peer is naming
hygiene, not a smaller install: `better-auth` already depends on zod, so
it stays in the tree of any app that uses `ramose/better-auth`.
//sideEffects: The `./src/**` globs are load-bearing in this workspace, not leftovers.
The root tsconfig `paths` point `ramose/worker` at `src/`, so the peer
Worker is bundled from source here even though only `dist` ships. Alchemy
re-exports `default` from a generated entry, so the Durable Object classes
reach the bundle only as re-exports — drop these globs and esbuild treats
the modules as side-effect-free and tree-shakes `TransactorDO` /
`QueryReplicaDO` away. Cloudflare then rejects the upload: "New version of
script does not export class 'QueryReplicaDO'". The `./dist/**` globs are
the same statement for a consumer bundling the published package.
